questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Every students (A) / in the class (B) / has passed the test. (C)
o: Part C: has passed the test.
questions.e: 'Every' is followed by a singular noun, so it should be 'Every student'. The verb 'has passed' is already singular.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Mumbai is larger (A) / than any other cities (B) / in Maharashtra. (C)
o: Part B: than any other cities
questions.e: After 'any other' a singular noun is needed: 'any other city'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Neither of the two boys (A) / were present (B) / in the class yesterday. (C)
o: Part A: Neither of the two boys
Part C: in the class yesterday.
questions.e: 'Neither of' takes a singular verb, so 'was present' is correct.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
I have been living in Delhi (A) / with my uncle (B) / since five years. (C)
o: Part A: I have been living in Delhi
questions.e: 'Since' is used with a point in time. A period of time takes 'for', so it should be 'for five years'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The furnitures in the hall (A) / are very old (B) / and need repair. (C)
o: Part A: The furnitures in the hall
questions.e: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form, so 'furnitures' is wrong. The correct phrase is 'the furniture'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
My brother works (A) / in a bank (B) / near our house. (C)
questions.e: The sentence is grammatically correct: the singular subject 'brother' takes 'works'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The teacher gave us (A) / many informations (B) / about the project. (C)
o: Part A: The teacher gave us
questions.e: 'Information' is uncountable and takes no plural. Use 'much information' or 'a lot of information'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Despite of her illness, (A) / she attended (B) / the meeting. (C)
o: Part A: Despite of her illness,
questions.e: 'Despite' is never followed by 'of'. The correct forms are 'despite her illness' or 'in spite of her illness'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Rahul and me (A) / went to the market (B) / to buy vegetables. (C)
o: Part B: went to the market
questions.e: A subject pronoun is needed: 'Rahul and I went'. 'Me' is the object form.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
She prefers tea (A) / in the morning (B) / than coffee. (C)
questions.e: 'Prefer' takes 'to', not 'than': 'prefers tea to coffee'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Hardly had he reached (A) / the station when (B) / the train left. (C)
o: Part A: Hardly had he reached
questions.e: 'Hardly had ... when' is a correct pair with inversion, and the past perfect is right. There is no error.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
One of the most important reason (A) / for the delay (B) / was heavy rain. (C)
o: Part A: One of the most important reason
questions.e: 'One of the' must be followed by a plural noun: 'one of the most important reasons'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
If I (A) / was the Prime Minister, (B) / I would ban plastic. (C)
o: Part B: was the Prime Minister,
Part C: I would ban plastic.
questions.e: An imaginary condition takes the subjunctive 'were' even for 'I': 'If I were the Prime Minister'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The number of students (A) / who have enrolled this year (B) / are higher than last year. (C)
o: Part A: The number of students
Part B: who have enrolled this year
Part C: are higher than last year.
questions.e: 'The number of' is singular, so the verb should be 'is higher'. 'A number of' would take a plural verb.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The manager, along with (A) / his assistants, are planning (B) / a surprise visit. (C)
o: Part A: The manager, along with
Part B: his assistants, are planning
questions.e: The verb agrees with the main subject 'manager', not with the phrase 'along with his assistants'. It should be 'is planning'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
No sooner I had seen (A) / the police than (B) / I ran away. (C)
o: Part A: No sooner I had seen
questions.e: After 'No sooner' the auxiliary comes before the subject: 'No sooner had I seen'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Unless you do not (A) / work hard, you (B) / will fail the test. (C)
o: Part A: Unless you do not
Part C: will fail the test.
questions.e: 'Unless' already means 'if ... not', so adding 'not' makes a double negative. It should be 'Unless you work hard'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
The jury has given (A) / its verdict after (B) / much deliberations. (C)
o: Part A: The jury has given
questions.e: 'Much' goes with an uncountable noun, so it should be 'much deliberation' (or 'long deliberations'). 'Jury ... its' is acceptable.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Scarcely had the speaker begun (A) / his speech than (B) / the lights went out. (C)
o: Part A: Scarcely had the speaker begun
Part C: the lights went out.
questions.e: 'Scarcely' (like 'hardly') pairs with 'when', not 'than'. 'No sooner' pairs with 'than'.

questions.q:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
Having finished his homework, (A) / the boy was allowed (B) / to go out and play. (C)
o: Part A: Having finished his homework,
Part B: the boy was allowed
Part C: to go out and play.
questions.e: The participle phrase correctly refers to the subject 'the boy', who finished the homework. The sentence has no error.
